episodes.203789: An anomalously hot and humid air mass was in place ahead of a cold front. Widespread showers and storms developed ahead of this front in a highly unstable environment with sufficient deep layer shear to lead to more organized multicell clusters. This led to scattered wind damage reports. In addition, with high PWATs, flash flooding developed in downtown Columbia.
episodes.203847: The monsoon high was centered across southeast Arizona and southwest New Mexico on August 1st and 2nd. Northwest flow around the upper high circulation along with embedded disturbances in this flow resulted in the development of showers and thunderstorms across parts of central and eastern New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours. Thunderstorms resulted in some flash flooding on and downstream of the Ruidoso burn scars and in Lincoln on August 1st and on and downstream of the Salt burn scar on August 2nd. Meanwhile, severe storms across northeast and east central New Mexico resulted in some large hail near Ocate, Miami, Sedan, Hayden, and Amistad. Severe thunderstorms also produced damaging wind gusts in Santa Rosa and Hayden.
episodes.204077: A line of thunderstorms produced widespread strong winds across the northeast Corner of Colorado across the counties of Logan, Phillips, and Sedgwick.
episodes.204115: Strong to occasionally severe thunderstorms track across northeast Colorado during the afternoon and evening hours of August 2nd.
episodes.204273: A persistent moist and unstable southwesterly flow aloft across the interior west ushered in precipitable water in excess of an inch for the first of August. Flow through the column was rather slow, resulting in thunderstorms that were slow to move and became anchored to outflow boundaries. A few strong gusts were observed, with a few instances of minor flooding across portions of the region.
episodes.204313: Atmospheric conditions allowed for efficient rainfall and severe thunderstorms.
episodes.204453: There were wind gusts in excess of 60 mph from showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.205168: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed in a summertime airmass with a couple of severe storms occurring in Lowndes county with impacts to trees and power lines.  In addition, a very moist airmass and weak steering flow led to flash flooding across portions of southwest Georgia.
episodes.205185: Thunderstorms developed across eastern Colorado and led to wind gusts up to 63 mph in Cheyenne county and up to 70 mph in Yuma county.
episodes.205186: Decaying thunderstorms across northwest Kansas led to a 67 mph wind gust at the Goodland Airport.
episodes.205214: An atypical early August backdoor cold front settled south through North Carolina, as a large cool area of high pressure centered over the Great Lakes nosed southward into central North Carolina. The passage of multiple upper level disturbances over eastern North America coupled with high moisture content and moderate instability supported numerous showers and storms. Sporadic downed trees and power lines and minor flooding were reported.
episodes.205331: A slow-moving front across south GA nudged southward. Frontal lift combined with very high moisture produced slow moving waves of locally heavy rainfall. A 'Slight' risk of heavy rainfall was outlooked by the Weather Prediction Center (Level 2 out of 4 levels).
episodes.205332: A slow-moving front across south GA nudged southward. Frontal lift combined with very high moisture produced slow moving waves of locally heavy rainfall. A 'Slight' risk of heavy rainfall was outlooked by the Weather Prediction Center (Level 2 out of 4 levels).
episodes.205369: Several severe thunderstorms moved across the area this day. The most imapctful storm hit Cheyenne where baseball sized hail was observed in the city of Cheyenne, WY.
episodes.205373: Severe Thunderstorm Watch issued for the southern Panhandle. Strong thunderstorm wind gusts occurred outside of the watch, mainly in Carbon and Albany Counties.
episodes.205391: Several large scale and small scale boundaries paired with near record moisture lead to a few severe wind gusts in thunderstorms.
episodes.205441: Anomalously high precipitable water (200-210% of normal) along with a shortwave trough, resulted in high rainfall rates with convection. The Weather Prediction Center issued a slight risk for excessive rainfall rates.
episodes.205805: A weak cool front drifted south through East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and extreme Northern Louisiana during the afternoon of August 1st, ahead of an upper level trough of low pressure that shifted east into the Four State Region. Large scale forcing along the front coupled with strong instability that developed in the moist air mass in place yielded scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across East Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon and evening, some of which became severe with locally heavy rainfall. Instances of damaging winds and localized flash flooding was observed across portions of East Texas, before the storms diminished during the evening with the loss of heating.
episodes.205842: Showers and thunderstorms affected northeast Tennessee and southwest Virginia during the afternoon and evening hours of August 2nd. Areas from Claiborne county, southeast through Greene and Cocke counties were affected the most. Some reports of flooding were received from Claiborne and Cocke counties.
episodes.205846: Showers and thunderstorms affected southwest Virginia and northeast Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of August 2nd. These produced some isolated flash flooding in southwest Virginia in the Wise area.
episodes.206131: Thunderstorms occurred across portions of western and central Wyoming on the afternoon of August 2nd. With large dew point depressions present, there were numerous reports of wind gusts of 58 mph or greater in Hot Springs, Washakie, and Sweetwater Counties. The highest wind gust reported was 71 mph to the east of Worland. In Hot Springs State Park near Thermopolis, law enforcement reported many tree branches downed.
episodes.206485: Several sites recorded greater than 58 mph thunderstorm winds.
episodes.206569: A weak cold front moved into and stalled across North Texas, serving as a focus for scattered shower and storm development over the first few days of August as upper level disturbances moved overtop the region. The storms were slow-moving and some became severe, producing damaging winds and hail. The highest wind gust occurred in the early morning hours of August 4th, when a microburst over the DFW ASOS produced an 89 mph wind gust (the strongest on record at that ASOS). Between the 1st and the 4th, there were many reports of damaging winds, and one report of 1 inch hail near Euless.
episodes.206592: Slow moving thunderstorms produced isolated areas of flash flooding.
episodes.206777: Thunderstorms produced gusty winds along the Brevard County coastline.
episodes.206829: A line of thunderstorms developed along a cold front in Central Texas and moved southward into South-Central Texas. Slow moving storms led to locally heavy rain that resulted in isolated flash flooding. One storm produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.206888: A weak warm front passing across the area encountered deep moisture, warm temperatures and large downdraft CAPE, favoring strong to severe thunderstorms across coastal waters.
episodes.206891: A weak warm front passing across the area encountered deep moisture and warm temperatures, favoring strong thunderstorms across Southeast South Carolina.
episodes.206892: A cold front along with mid-level energy shifting across the region encountered a warm and moist environment, favoring strong to severe thunderstorms across Southeast Georgia.
episodes.207056: A few severe developed and brough some large hail and a few damaging wind gusts to the area.
episodes.207150: A tropical wave, southeasterly flow and abundant tropical moisture over the islands promoted t-storm formation. A lightning strike impacted electrical lines in Aibonito, causing a utility pole to fall and result in a power outage.
episodes.207226: A cold front moving south through the region stalled as it reached the Louisiana coast during the afternoon hours. The boundary served as a focus for scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop over the nearshore waters. With ample low-level moisture and weak surface convergence along the boundary, conditions were favorable for the development of waterspouts. Multiple reports and videos from the public and social media confirmed waterspouts forming offshore of the Louisiana coastline. In one notable instance, a video captured four waterspouts occurring simultaneously over the coastal waters before dissipating. No damage or injuries were reported.
